nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor d1 (spec 0003 index.md:780, :855): row k of walk 3 keeps writes open when the second primary is a quarantined node, against the letter of PRD-006 AC-2, and the PRD does not say so; fix: add the exception or a dated note to PRD-006 AC-2
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor d1 (spec 0003 index.md:780, :855): row k of walk 3 keeps writes open when the second primary is a quarantined node, against the letter of prd-006 ac-2, and the prd does not say so; fix: add the exception or a dated note to prd-006 ac-2
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: add the exception to PRD-006 AC-2, or a dated note under it that points to spec 0003, and say in the spec that rule 10 leaves quarantined nodes out on purpose, so that scope 010 knows the exception also covers a quarantined node on a later timeline.The document reviewer rated this major; the main reviewer rates it minor. The decision is written down and reasoned (decision 17, heavy) and judged right: the quarantine is the reviewed answer to exactly that node, closing would let one returned old primary stop a cluster after a correct promotion, and POOL sends nothing to the quarantined node either way. What is missing is one sentence where the requirement lives. docs/prd/ is not a file a sub session may change, so this is for the lead. Owner: the lead and the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m1 (admission.rs:182, authority.rs:137): a Ready state cannot learn of a conflict latch set after the start, so writes reopen once the second primary drops out of sight; fix: a spec 0003 decision before scope 004 plus a walk from row d to row o
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m1 (admission.rs:182, authority.rs:137): a ready state cannot learn of a conflict latch set after the start, so writes reopen once the second primary drops out of sight; fix: a spec 0003 decision before scope 004 plus a walk from row d to row o
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: decide it in spec 0003 before scope 004 dispatches SQL (a new item of Follow-up 4 or a criterion next to AC-16): either a pool-control function that takes a Ready state and a Closed that asks for the latch and returns the state with the latch set, or a rule that the daemon reads and classifies the journal again after every write, plus the memory for a failed write; then add a walk from row d to row o through the real functions, with the second primary gone in the second call.This is the case R-19 and PRD-006 AC-2 are about: the other primary is still there, it just cannot be seen any more, and writes open again. It is the same kind of gap as the one 0003 AC-16 closed, where the function trusted its caller. Nothing calls the function yet, so nothing is wrong today; it will be wrong on the first day of scope 004 unless that slice adds the missing piece inside pool-control. The same holds for the authority revision in an Open answer. Owner: the architect for the spec, then the developer.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m2 (authority.rs:18, :35): StoreProbe, StoredAuthority, ApprovedTopology and Quarantine have public fields, so any crate can build a journal value and 0003 AC-12 holds only by convention; fix: private fields or a W3/W5 line in scope 004
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m2 (authority.rs:18, :35): storeprobe, storedauthority, approvedtopology and quarantine have public fields, so any crate can build a journal value and 0003 ac-12 holds only by convention; fix: private fields or a w3/w5 line in scope 004
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: when scope 004 puts the journal reader inside pool-control, make the fields private and give the tests one constructor that runs the same checks as the reader, or add a line to rule W3 or W5 that keeps StoreProbe::Present out of every other crate; record the choice in Follow-up 4.AC-12 shows that Authority, EligiblePrimary, Closed and BootstrapPlan cannot be built outside the crate, but with a free StoreProbe that proof does not carry far: the one thing that turns into authority is the thing anyone can make. Today only tests do. The spec names the condition (the journal reader stays the only code that builds a StoreProbe) and no check enforces it. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m3 (observation.rs:140): a latest sample dated after now, or two samples tied at the latest time, count as no evidence, which hides a seen second primary on a node other than the writer; fix: a spec decision for scope 004 on the caller's duty
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m3 (observation.rs:140): a latest sample dated after now, or two samples tied at the latest time, count as no evidence, which hides a seen second primary on a node other than the writer; fix: a spec decision for scope 004 on the caller's duty
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: the smallest is a duty of the caller, written into the documentation comment of writer_admission and into Follow-up 4 (read now after the list of observations is fixed, pass at most one sample per node); a stricter one is in the rule itself: for a node other than the writer, a latest sample that cannot be used closes with a reason of its own.Both inputs can happen in scope 004 without anyone doing something strange: a probe result that lands a moment after the daemon read now is in the future of now, and two probe paths handing in the same sample tie. In both cases one admission can open while a second primary is in the list. Owner: the architect.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m4 (tools/repo-check/src/workspace.rs:236): the W4 lockfile check is passed by a [[patch.unused]] table after the last local package, the test at :1210 pins that and prove-checks.sh has no case for it; fix: end an entry at any line starting with [
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m4 (tools/repo-check/src/workspace.rs:236): the w4 lockfile check is passed by a [[patch.unused]] table after the last local package, the test at :1210 pins that and prove-checks.sh has no case for it; fix: end an entry at any line starting with [
nodes.rationale: Suggested fix: end an entry at any line that starts with [ (a lockfile entry never holds a table of its own), change the sentence in spec 0003 and the pinned test with it, add one prove-checks.sh case that adds a local package to the lockfile and expects W4, and soften 'closes finding m14' in the spec 0002 note until then.The check exists for one case, a package Cargo treats as a member without being listed; that case still needs a change to the W1 baseline, which a reviewer sees, so the risk is small. But a guard with a known way around it and a test that calls the way around correct will be trusted more than it should be. Owner: the architect for the two sentences, the developer for the rest.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m5 (topology.rs:399, report.rs:139): one file at the size limit (349514 empty identity entries) gives 2097084 findings, up to 251 MB of output and 539 MB of memory; fix: a BufWriter in check_config, then a spec decision on a findings limit
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m5 (topology.rs:399, report.rs:139): one file at the size limit (349514 empty identity entries) gives 2097084 findings, up to 251 mb of output and 539 mb of memory; fix: a bufwriter in check_config, then a spec decision on a findings limit
nodes.rationale: Measured with the debug build on a file of 1048574 bytes: the human format wrote 190709698 bytes in 2.5 seconds with a peak of 405 MB, the JSON format 251525214 bytes in 8.5 seconds with a peak of 539 MB; the time is linear and each human finding is one system call through the line buffered stdout lock (main.rs:77). Suggested fix: wrap the locked stdout in a BufWriter in check_config, then decide in the spec whether the number of findings gets a limit (one config.missing_key per entry with no key at all, or a fixed top count with a last line).The file belongs to the operator, so this is not an attack, but it is the same function the daemon will call at a start and at a reload, and bounded resources then means about 500 times the input. AC-15 bounds the time for the made inputs and says nothing about the number of findings. A limit changes AC-3, so it is the architect's call. Owner: the developer for the buffer, the architect for the limit.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor m6 (admission.rs:238, :288, observation.rs:143): the cost of one writer admission grows with nodes times observations while the configuration allows about 13000 nodes; fix in scope 004: answer from the snapshot or index observations by node
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m6 (admission.rs:238, :288, observation.rs:143): the cost of one writer admission grows with nodes times observations while the configuration allows about 13000 nodes; fix in scope 004: answer from the snapshot or index observations by node
nodes.rationale: Each call walks every node of the file, builds two lists and walks every observation for every node of the cluster; the member check at admission.rs:257 is members times nodes. Suggested fix: when scope 004 wires it, answer admission from the topology snapshot and call the function only when the configuration, the journal or an observation changes, or index the observations by node once; say which in the spec of scope 004.With three nodes it is nothing, but spec 0003 has scope 004 call the function at every session admission and again after the backend is acquired, the root guide asks for bounded work on the data path, and the validation time rule of the spec covers validate only. Owner: the architect of scope 004.

nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor m8 (topology.rs:456): names accept the control characters u+0080 to u+009f and direction characters such as u+202e, pinned by the test at topology.rs:894; fix: a spec decision before a name reaches any output (refuse them, or escape on output)

U+009B is an escape lead on some terminals, and a direction override makes two entries look alike on a screen. Owner: the architect.

nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor t1 (topology.rs:688): no test fails when the config.duplicate_id check for cluster.id is removed from cross_check (all 238 tests still pass; the code is right); fix: a test with two [[cluster]] entries of one id and one pinning the order of step 6.1

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t2 (topology.rs:728, :731, :772): three skip rules of the cross checks are pinned by no test (a bad cluster id, a node with a bad cluster, the endpoint check on a node whose port failed); fix: three small cases in tests/validate.rs
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor t2 (topology.rs:728, :731, :772): three skip rules of the cross checks are pinned by no test (a bad cluster id, a node with a bad cluster, the endpoint check on a node whose port failed); fix: three small cases in tests/validate.rs
nodes.rationale: The three changes every test survived: skipping the expected_writer check for all clusters when one cluster has a bad id, running that check although a node has a bad cluster, and letting the endpoint check read a node whose port failed (AC-15 made input 3). Suggested fix: two clusters where one has a bad id and the other a wrong writer; a writer whose node has a bad cluster; two nodes with the same host and port = 0.These are the rules that make one mistake give one finding (AC-2). They were reworded after the verification of milestone 2, so they are the part of the validation order most likely to be touched again. Owner: the tester.

nodes.label: Scope 003 review Minor t3 (admission.rs:89, pool-config lib.rs:44): the compile_fail,E0451 documentation tests do not check the error code on Rust 1.100.0 (E0308 also passed) although verify.md:206 says so; fix: correct verify.md and pair each with a passing test
nodes.norm_label: scope 003 review minor t3 (admission.rs:89, pool-config lib.rs:44): the compile_fail,e0451 documentation tests do not check the error code on rust 1.100.0 (e0308 also passed) although verify.md:206 says so; fix: correct verify.md and pair each with a passing test
nodes.rationale: The four pool-control tests are at admission.rs:89, :137, authority.rs:128 and bootstrap.rs:57; the older ValidatedConfig test (lib.rs:44) names three of what are now eight fields, so it fails for the missing fields and would keep failing if the fields became public. Suggested fix: correct the sentence in verify.md, use the update form ValidatedConfig { config_version: 2, ..valid } whose only possible error is the private field, and add a passing documentation test beside each compile_fail test that uses the same paths through the public functions.These tests are the proof of the second half of AC-12 and of the AC-3 rule that validate is the only way to a ValidatedConfig. Each still catches the real mistake as long as its snippet has no other error; a renamed field or type turns it into a test that passes for the wrong reason, without a sign. nodes.label: Seven required checks
nodes.rationale: Every pull request must pass the same named checks available through scripts/check.sh.

nodes.label: Conflict latch persistence
nodes.rationale: Controller writes later conflicts durably because startup Ready authority does not update itself.

nodes.label: Single SQLite writer
nodes.rationale: Only journal.rs touches files or names rusqlite; mutable write methods enforce one connection owner.

nodes.label: R-05 incorrect reuse or late cancel
nodes.norm_label: r-05 incorrect reuse or late cancel
nodes.rationale: Critical risk mitigated by lease generations, quarantine and race/model tests.

nodes.label: Credential generation retirement
nodes.rationale: Owners retain their connections until release; old waiters and handshakes cannot receive stale leases.

nodes.label: Independent safety review
nodes.rationale: Protocol, authentication, parser and failover work requires the appropriate independent review.

nodes.label: Explicit observation time
nodes.rationale: Caller supplies time; future, stale or tied latest samples are rejected as evidence.

nodes.label: Bounded safe Rust
nodes.rationale: Explicit ownership, typed errors, bounded buffers/queues/tasks and no uncontrolled panics protect hot-path safety.

nodes.label: Invalid reload retains safe generation
nodes.rationale: A failed reload leaves the previous safe generation active.

nodes.label: No uncertain replay
nodes.rationale: Once bytes may have reached PostgreSQL, never replay a statement or transaction, including a lost COMMIT response.

nodes.label: Production release boundary
nodes.rationale: Extended protocol, cancellation forwarding, replica sessions, administration, failover and cache remain planned; no supported production release or public performance result.

nodes.label: R-03 session state leakage
nodes.rationale: Critical cross-identity risk mitigated with identity keys, pinned leases and close-on-uncertain reset.

nodes.label: Conservative reusable profile
nodes.rationale: No forwarded startup settings; bounded built-in operations only; uncertain cleanup closes the backend.

nodes.label: Graphify before commit
nodes.rationale: Refresh the graph after the last edit so the same commit includes a graph reflecting changed files.

nodes.label: Verified primary invariant
nodes.rationale: Writes require verified primary authority; health failure alone never authorizes promotion.

nodes.label: Uncertain dispatched work
nodes.rationale: Lost statement outcome yields 08007 and ends the session without replay.

nodes.label: Drain, attach and quarantine operations
nodes.rationale: A successful probe cannot clear an operator's maintenance, detach or quarantine decision.

nodes.label: ApprovedTopology
nodes.rationale: Durable approved writer, epoch and quarantine represent authorization; observed role does not substitute for it.

nodes.label: FenceReceipt
nodes.rationale: Operation-bound independent verification of fencing includes machine identity and expiry.

nodes.label: All-writer write barrier
nodes.rationale: A final flush target can only be claimed after a barrier covering every writer path, including connections that bypass POOL; draining POOL alone is insufficient.

nodes.label: Candidate and RPO policy
nodes.rationale: Highest LSN alone cannot establish that every acknowledged commit survived; no zero data loss claim is inferred from asynchronous replication.

nodes.label: Fencing contract (allowlisted adapter)
nodes.rationale: A successful power off request is insufficient without verified completion and exclusion from automatic restart or another writer path.

nodes.label: Promotion operation stages (Plan, Quiesce, Fence, Revalidate, Promote, Reconcile, Recover)
nodes.norm_label: promotion operation stages (plan, quiesce, fence, revalidate, promote, reconcile, recover)

nodes.label: Fresh observation authority agreement
nodes.rationale: Admission combines a durable authorization decision with fresh authenticated node facts.

nodes.label: Restore reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Restored authority keeps writes closed until independent evidence reconciles quarantine and external effects.

nodes.label: Manual failover policy
nodes.rationale: A transport timeout or failed health probe never authorizes promotion; PostgreSQL requires preventing the former primary from returning as another primary.

nodes.label: Daemon credential snapshot
nodes.rationale: daemon.rs reads a complete protected snapshot and calls Server::rotate_credentials.

nodes.label: Daemon task supervision
nodes.rationale: supervise watches control, probe, listener and log tasks; shutdown revokes credential publication authority.

nodes.label: Four command composition
nodes.rationale: check-config is offline; bootstrap creates authority, show-authority reports it, and run composes core/control/probe/log tasks.

nodes.label: Atomic runtime generation
nodes.rationale: pool.rs owns generations and FIFO; rotate_credentials publishes a complete snapshot atomically.

nodes.label: Expected generation precondition
nodes.rationale: Mutation names its compared generation and rejects preconditions invalidated by intervening changes.

nodes.label: Redacted JSON command output
nodes.rationale: Constant text, schema keys and numbers prevent secrets or parser/OS messages from reaching output.

nodes.label: Authority revision
nodes.rationale: Durable counter for approved topology, quarantine, membership or restore-hold changes.

nodes.label: Credential generation
nodes.rationale: Version of a secret reference; rotation retires the old generation.

nodes.label: Eligible primary
nodes.rationale: Approved writer whose fresh observation agrees; only this node receives writes.

nodes.label: Lease
nodes.rationale: Exclusive ownership of a backend by one frontend for the whole session.

nodes.label: Pool key
nodes.rationale: Full backend identity partitions reusable connections.

nodes.label: Writer admission agreement
nodes.rationale: Configuration expected_writer, durable approved writer and fresh observation must agree or admission closes.

nodes.label: Physical permit lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Returned connections retain their original physical permits through cleanup and idle.

nodes.label: R-13 memory exhaustion
nodes.rationale: Global byte/task/queue budgets require slow-reader and many-key validation.

nodes.label: R-19 restart wrong writer
nodes.rationale: Durable approved writer and fresh matching observations mitigate restart adoption; raw journal/VM rollback remains exposure.

nodes.label: R-25 reviewer unavailable
nodes.rationale: A review gate stays open and cannot be self-approved when reviewer or lab is unavailable.

nodes.label: All state backend budgets
nodes.rationale: Connecting, leased, cleaning and idle connections count against backend budgets.

nodes.label: Status follows evidence
nodes.rationale: Failed or unrun criteria remain visible and cannot become release claims.

nodes.rationale: Lag thresholds screen new session admission only; an LSN based causal token is deferred rather than approximated by a time based sticky window.

nodes.label: Operator managed principal to backend login map
nodes.norm_label: operator managed principal to backend login map
nodes.rationale: Unmapped combinations fail; startup strings alone cannot select credentials.

nodes.label: SQL classification through PostgreSQL 18 raw grammar
nodes.norm_label: sql classification through postgresql 18 raw grammar
nodes.rationale: Classification is not an authorization engine; views, rules, RLS, functions and FDW side effects cannot be proven safe by a raw AST.

nodes.label: Session pooling (one frontend owns one backend lease)
nodes.norm_label: session pooling (one frontend owns one backend lease)
nodes.rationale: First safe mode because it preserves a real backend session throughout a client connection; it gives less backend reduction than transaction multiplexing and that limit is accepted explicitly.

nodes.label: No automatic retry after dispatch
nodes.rationale: Once query bytes may have been sent the outcome is uncertain, so a backend failure surfaces as connection loss or the real server error; only initial acquisition before ReadyForQuery may pick another endpoint.

nodes.label: Login time backend selection on pinned lease
nodes.norm_label: login time backend selection on pinned lease
nodes.rationale: The backend is chosen from profile and fresh topology before SQL is available; the parser is not an input to initial selection and later operations are admitted or rejected without changing endpoint.

nodes.label: No primary fallback for replica profiles
nodes.norm_label: no primary fallback for replica profiles
nodes.rationale: A future primary fallback would need independently enforced read restrictions that survive role changes and a new explicit decision.

nodes.label: No silent replay of uncertain work (lost COMMIT response)
nodes.norm_label: no silent replay of uncertain work (lost commit response)
nodes.rationale: If the backend response is lost after COMMIT, the client observes connection loss; POOL never retries or reports a definite rollback.

nodes.label: Generation checked journaled mutations
nodes.rationale: Mutations are journaled with caller, idempotency key and expected generation so conflicting requests against one generation yield at most one effect; failure to persist intent prevents the external action.

nodes.label: Durable intent before fencing and reconciliation of unknown outcomes
nodes.norm_label: durable intent before fencing and reconciliation of unknown outcomes
nodes.rationale: Lost responses can cause unsafe repeated operations; an inconclusive result keeps admission closed and prevents a second irreversible action.

nodes.label: RPO disclosure: known flush target or unknown loss window
nodes.norm_label: rpo disclosure: known flush target or unknown loss window
nodes.rationale: No implied zero data loss under asynchronous replication; switching to an unknown loss window requires a new plan and explicit approval.

nodes.label: Authenticated management transport (protected local or mTLS)
nodes.norm_label: authenticated management transport (protected local or mtls)
nodes.rationale: No unauthenticated loopback assumption: local port access is not identity; remote binding requires mTLS and explicit configuration.

nodes.label: Administration mutation retry contract
nodes.rationale: Retries resolve by actor, action and request ID; the same request returns the original operation ID even after lost response or restart, and reuse with a different target or payload conflicts, so one accepted request yields one logical operation.

nodes.label: Shared conventions
nodes.rationale: Keys, output, redaction, typed IDs/generations and generated SQLSTATEs have one owner rather than per-slice reinvention.

nodes.label: Inventory Coverage Limits
nodes.rationale: The inventory does not audit every C path, alias, build flag or regression. Excluded features remain visible rather than being removed from the denominator.

nodes.label: Pgpool-II 4.7.3 Baseline
nodes.rationale: The baseline distinguishes reference behavior from POOL additions. The inventory is a planning corpus, not 100 percent parity; every capability is Research or Planned.

nodes.label: Decisions before implementation (planning ledger): each safety sensitive feature still gets a scoped build specification with concrete defaults, interfaces, acceptance criteria and source values; the PRDs are proposed product contracts; a new choice that changes a ratified safety contract amends the governing decision and links the superseding spec in the ledger before building against it

nodes.label: Release Practices
nodes.rationale: Milestone names are gates, not version numbers, and a version number is not a safety certification. Reverting binaries or TOML cannot undo a promotion or silently restore stale writer authority.

nodes.label: Cross Check Before Development
nodes.rationale: Every document was read against the others and against the workflow steps; the pass assigns single owners for shared conventions, terms, statuses, tooling choices and release packaging. It changes documents only and approves no feature.

nodes.label: Development Readiness Review
nodes.rationale: The review changes the plan and proposed acceptance cases; it does not record feature approval or implementation.

nodes.label: Validation Limits
nodes.rationale: No executable proxy exists and nothing was built or run; counts and link checks do not establish software correctness.

nodes.label: F-018 CancelRequest and BackendKeyData
nodes.rationale: Virtual per lease keys, serialized retirement, close backend after forwarded cancellation so a late cancel cannot target a reused lease.

nodes.label: Critical Path Handoffs
nodes.rationale: Handoffs are the points where an assumption by one engineer could invalidate another engineer's work. Start dependent behavior only once the evidence or decision it uses is available; the first write needs durable approved writer identity and fresh matching observations, and without verified fencing manual promotion cannot qualify.

nodes.label: CancellationEntry
nodes.rationale: Per lease opaque frontend token; real backend key data stays private and memory only.

nodes.label: PoolKey
nodes.rationale: Partition by full backend identity and configuration/credential generations so keys preserve actual database login identity.

nodes.label: Cancellation dispatch to the session-owning proxy
nodes.norm_label: cancellation dispatch to the session-owning proxy

nodes.label: Retry only before initial lease and ReadyForQuery exposure
nodes.norm_label: retry only before initial lease and readyforquery exposure
nodes.rationale: Acquisition retry wording could imply session replacement; never retry after established session loss.

nodes.label: Private backend keys and virtual frontend cancellation credentials
nodes.norm_label: private backend keys and virtual frontend cancellation credentials
nodes.rationale: Cancellation could arrive after lease reuse; serialize retirement and close the physical backend after forwarding.

nodes.label: Terminated SCRAM over TLS with optional mTLS and separate backend credentials
nodes.norm_label: terminated scram over tls with optional mtls and separate backend credentials
nodes.rationale: Confirmed boundary: frontend authentication is terminated at the proxy and backend credentials are separately provisioned. The first implementation is designed in spec 0004: SCRAM against a verifier file per principal, with no channel binding yet; client certificates and channel binding wait for scope 006.

nodes.label: Bounded admission, deadlines and graceful teardown
nodes.norm_label: bounded admission, deadlines and graceful teardown
nodes.rationale: Correctness and identity isolation precede throughput; all queues, buffers, tasks and external calls have explicit budgets.

nodes.label: Cancellation forwarded only through the live lease owner
nodes.norm_label: cancellation forwarded only through the live lease owner
nodes.rationale: Serialize cancellation with retirement and retire the physical backend after forwarding so later clients cannot be affected.

nodes.label: Reset and validate before reuse; close uncertain state
nodes.norm_label: reset and validate before reuse; close uncertain state
nodes.rationale: Unsafe reuse can leak identity or session state; reset uncertainty closes the socket instead of returning it idle.

nodes.label: Session pooling only (no transaction or statement multiplexing in V1)
nodes.norm_label: session pooling only (no transaction or statement multiplexing in v1)
nodes.rationale: Reuse clean backend sessions without changing the lifetime semantics of a connected frontend; one backend per connected frontend.

nodes.label: Proposed protocol limits (64 KiB startup, 16 MiB message)
nodes.norm_label: proposed protocol limits (64 kib startup, 16 mib message)

nodes.label: SCRAM channel binding per terminated TLS channel
nodes.norm_label: scram channel binding per terminated tls channel

nodes.label: Variable length cancellation keys (protocol 3.2, up to 256 bytes)
nodes.norm_label: variable length cancellation keys (protocol 3.2, up to 256 bytes)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding the historical four byte key is incorrect.

nodes.label: Rust tokio-postgres and postgres drivers (MVP gate)
nodes.norm_label: rust tokio-postgres and postgres drivers (mvp gate)

nodes.label: Features outside the initial support claim
nodes.norm_label: features outside the initial support claim
nodes.rationale: Protocol 2, legacy MD5, GSS, OAuth, logical replication clients and arbitrary extensions are excluded until qualified; a refused unsupported feature is different from silent corruption.

nodes.label: Proposed stopping rules
nodes.rationale: If parser coverage fails, route to primary or disable routing; if a session cannot be reset confidently, close the backend; if fencing cannot be verified, do not promote; fix measured bottlenecks before adding policies.

nodes.label: Close uncertain sessions cleanup policy
nodes.rationale: Unknown extension state may survive a nominal reset, so the default closes uncertain sessions with a positive allowlist for reusable profiles.

nodes.label: Independent backend credentials per mapped login identity
nodes.norm_label: independent backend credentials per mapped login identity
nodes.rationale: SCRAM verifier authentication on the frontend does not recover a reusable backend password; a global privileged role with SET ROLE is outside the initial contract.

nodes.label: Virtual per lease cancellation keys
nodes.rationale: Session manager owns virtual per lease frontend keys, keeps real backend keys private, serializes dispatch with retirement and closes the physical backend after a forwarded cancellation so there is no cross lease effect.

nodes.label: Deterministic derivation and post handoff retirement tests
nodes.norm_label: deterministic derivation and post handoff retirement tests

nodes.label: Inspected final evidence: 36 PostgreSQL integration cases passed
nodes.norm_label: inspected final evidence: 36 postgresql integration cases passed

nodes.label: Bounded cleanup and immutable startup attestation
nodes.norm_label: bounded cleanup and immutable startup attestation
nodes.rationale: Cleanup must prove the original baseline rather than trust state left by the previous owner.

nodes.label: Nested physical budgets reserved under one pool mutex
nodes.norm_label: nested physical budgets reserved under one pool mutex
nodes.rationale: Permits travel with the physical connection, and cancellation drops the ticket and wakes the queue.

nodes.label: Deliberately wrong changes prove checks reject regressions
nodes.norm_label: deliberately wrong changes prove checks reject regressions
nodes.rationale: A green result is trustworthy only when a representative broken rule is shown to fail.

nodes.label: Routing decision: primary default, explicit read only session profiles
nodes.norm_label: routing decision: primary default, explicit read only session profiles
nodes.rationale: Endpoint chosen at login, SQL admitted on pinned lease, lag screened at admission only, eventual reads, no primary fallback. Arbitrary sessions never move between servers; continuous staleness guarantees and transparent mixed-session routing are deferred.

nodes.label: SQLite journal for operations, audit and approved writer/epoch/quarantine
nodes.norm_label: sqlite journal for operations, audit and approved writer/epoch/quarantine
nodes.rationale: Local persistence stores durable authorization but never observed backend role truth; bootstrap once and reconcile with fresh roles before restart admission. The records, the journal format and the start rules are settled in spec 0003; the journal file, the bootstrap command and the probe are designed in spec 0004.

nodes.label: Approved writer, epoch and quarantine authority
nodes.norm_label: approved writer, epoch and quarantine authority
nodes.rationale: Immutable snapshots publish only when fresh observed roles agree with durable authorization; conflicting config or observations cannot silently change authority.
